name: Heat a shelter
summary: Heat people, not air. Shrink the space: one small insulated room, or a tent pitched inside a room, holds heat a whole house can’t. A sheet-metal wood stove with a proper flue heats it safely, and any flame indoors needs a carbon monoxide alarm. Electric heat is too hungry for scavenged power, but a 12V heated blanket warms a bed on about 50W.

parts.why: Holds heat in the room you live in
Stove bodies, flue pipe and heat shields
A tent inside a room, door curtains and draught blocks
Sleeping pads and draught seals: cold ground steals heat
Fuel for indoor-rated heaters, used with ventilation
12V blankets and pads warm a person, not a room

tips: Fit a battery CO alarm wherever anything burns indoors. Most homes have one on a wall or ceiling.
Never burn charcoal, or run a generator or BBQ grill, indoors.
Insulate under you first: a good sleeping pad matters as much as the bag.
A metal bottle of hot water in a sleeping bag stays warm for hours.
Leave a small vent open even in the cold: a stove needs air in and fumes out.
